subject: general
question: In 1947, the Indian economy was marked by deep poverty. Which sector dominated the Indian economy at the time of independence?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Agricultural sector**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 1947, the Indian economy was predominantly agrarian, with more than 70% of the population engaged in agricultural activities.
 
• The agricultural sector contributed the largest share to the Indian GDP at the time of independence, highlighting its dominance in the economy.
 
• Despite its significance, agriculture was underdeveloped, marked by low productivity, outdated techniques, and dependence on monsoons.
 
• The sector faced challenges due to colonial policies, which prioritized cash crops for export rather than food crops for domestic consumption.
 
• Additionally, land ownership was skewed, with the zamindari system creating inequities among farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Sector:**

 
 
• The industrial sector was relatively small in 1947, contributing only a minor share to India's GDP.
 
• Most industries were concentrated in urban areas and focused on textiles, jute, and basic consumer goods.
 
• India lacked heavy industries, as the colonial government discouraged industrialization to maintain dependence on British imports.
 
• Post-independence efforts focused on expanding this sector, particularly through the establishment of public sector enterprises.
 
 
 
• **Services Sector:**
 
 
• The services sector, which includes trade, transportation, and administration, was not a significant contributor to the economy at the time of independence.
 
• Its contribution to GDP was minimal compared to agriculture and industry.
 
• The growth in this sector accelerated in later decades, driven by advancements in IT, telecommunications, and financial services.
 
 
 
• **Manufacturing Sector:**
 
 
• The manufacturing sector was underdeveloped during colonial rule, and its contribution to the economy was limited.
 
• Small-scale industries dominated manufacturing, with little technological innovation.
 
• Post-independence, the Indian government focused on building a robust manufacturing base, particularly through the establishment of heavy industries and industrial policies.
